blocks.x: Decision hubs beat model sprawl — an Achala delivery-floor perspective. Written by the practice that ran the work: what shipped, what scaled and the vendor questions worth asking before you commit.
Decision hubs beat model sprawl, the argument in one line. Separability (models score, policy decides, humans supervise) survives audit and staff turnover.
Champion-challenger discipline makes model risk a measured, improving quantity.
Decision replay converts regulatory questions from expeditions into queries.

Where decision hubs beat model sprawl breaks in practice: autonomy granted faster than governance, agents shipped with policies nobody wrote down and telemetry nobody reads, until the incident review becomes the real policy meeting.

decision hubs beat model sprawl has a serious opposition, and it goes: the policy-first thesis can ossify into approvals that cost more than the work. Autonomy tiers need revisiting on a cadence, not once at launch.
The practice, as we run it

In delivery, decision hubs beat model sprawl becomes a specific discipline: the build is a governed agent fleet: policies that bound what each agent may do, telemetry that shows what it did, and replay for when anyone asks why. Every program in the Agentic AI & Hyperautomation domain carries the same obligations, a signed baseline, named gate criteria, and evidence generated by running the system rather than preparing for a meeting.
Bring decision hubs beat model sprawl to a 45-minute briefing with the practice lead, your metric, our method, and an honest read on feasibility.
